claims.claim: Repository-centered peer review with social-network reviewer selection predates TDRG.
claims.source_locator: Rodriguez et al. abstract and system description
claims.evidence: The source describes an OAI-PMH peer-review service using a social-network algorithm to select reviewers and weight evaluations.
claims.notes: Bounded prior-art claim; not an exhaustive priority search.

claims.claim: Fair/randomized reviewer assignment and global, root-relative, and local graph trust are prior work rather than TDRG inventions.
claims.evidence: The sources respectively define fair assignment, randomized assignment, global recursive reputation, root-relative max-flow trust, and local trust evaluation.
claims.notes: No transfer of performance claims from prior domains to TDRG.

claims.claim: Anonymous review and anonymous reputation mechanisms predate TDRG.
claims.source_locator: Naessens et al. abstract; AnonRep abstract
claims.evidence: The sources present anonymous credential-based submission/review with accountability and tracking-resistant anonymous reputation, respectively.
claims.notes: Threat models differ; neither source validates TDRG.

claims.claim: The draft TDRG profile defines typed shared scientific/review events separately from root-, topic-, capability-, policy-, and time-relative views and prohibits a universal actor score.
claims.evidence: The local normative draft explicitly states the separation and invariants.
claims.notes: A design-definition claim, not evidence of benefit.

claims.claim: Eleven unit tests passed in a local rerun of tooling revision 9da0cd433147d925bac4ae1e1f94186cc4166e7b on 2026-08-24.
claims.evidence: unittest reported Ran 11 tests and OK; revision was read with git rev-parse HEAD.
claims.notes: Local, synthetic, non-archival, and not independently rerun.

claims.claim: The v0.1 replay test establishes equality of Python result objects after reversing one fixture's event order, not cross-platform canonical byte identity.
claims.evidence: The test reverses events, evaluates twice, and calls assertEqual on the result objects.

claims.claim: The v0.1 artifact does not implement signatures, uniqueness, Sybil/collusion defenses, case personas, appeals/opening, fork reconciliation, standards round trips, rollback, or A0--A4 comparison.
claims.source_locator: Repository source/test/schema inventory and docs/architecture.md explicit non-properties
claims.evidence: The inspected revision contains evaluator/resource modules, one view schema, two examples, and one 11-test file; architecture documentation names these non-properties.

claims.claim: Named conformance behavior does not establish reviewer competence, anonymity beyond a threat model, scientific correctness, or community benefit.
claims.source_locator: Conformance tuple and protocol conformance limits
claims.evidence: Conformance binds code, fixtures, policy, and outputs; excluded properties require separate security, scientific, or field evidence.

claims.claim: NISO, COAR Notify, DocMaps, Crossref, PROV-O, and RO-Crate cover portions of review terminology, exchange, event description, registration, provenance, and research-object packaging.
claims.source_locator: Official specifications/documentation and RO-Crate primary article
claims.evidence: Each official source states the corresponding bounded function; no source is claimed to implement TDRG policy.
claims.notes: Standards freshness checked 2026-08-24; no TM-16 projection exists.

claims.claim: A3/A4 outperform A0--A2 under the preregistered capture, leakage, dissent, fork, and privacy measures.
claims.evidence: No A0--A4 implementation, frozen dataset, seed manifest, or result report exists.
claims.notes: Retained only as H1--H6 open hypotheses; no result prose.

claims.claim: The proposed fresh case-persona design provides anonymity, unlinkability, duplicate resistance, and accountable opening.
claims.evidence: Prior systems show related mechanisms, but no TDRG persona implementation or threat-model test exists.
claims.notes: Removed as a result claim; manuscript specifies desired semantics and downgrade rule only.

claims.claim: The v0.1 resource classifier preserves multiple resource axes and requires excluded claims for non-full modes in the named fixtures.
claims.evidence: Three tests exercise R2 labeling with preserved human hours, rejection of empty exclusions for a non-full mode, and R0 labeling for a lightweight profile.
claims.notes: Thresholds are prototype policy, not a validated standard.

claims.claim: TDRG improves scientific validity or peer-review outcomes in independently governed communities.
claims.evidence: No field deployment or independent-community outcome study exists.
claims.notes: Explicitly excluded throughout; reserved for a later ethically governed study.
